slides.title: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
slides.description:
Role of the EEOC is to protect employees from unfair treatment

The laws prohibit discrimination, harassment, retaliation and various other practices

Protected Classes under the Human Rights Law Title VII:

  • Age
  • Immigration or citizenship status
  • Color
  • Disability
  • Gender (including sexual harassment)
  • Gender Identity
  • Marital status and partnership status
  • National origin

slides.title: Race/color discrimination
slides.description:
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act includes:

  • Equal Pay Act
  • Age Discrimination
  • American Disabilities Act
  • Civil Rights Act
  • Protects individuals against employment discrimination based on race and color as well as cannot deny employment due to perceived race-linked characteristics
  • It is unlawful to discriminated against any individual in regard to recruiting, hiring, promotion, transfer, work assignments, performance measurements, job training, discipline and discharge, wages and benefits, or any other term or condition or employment

slides.title: Race related or hostile work environment
slides.description:
Prohibits offensive conduct such as racial or ethnic slurs racial jokes, derogatory comments or other verbal or physical conduct based on an individuals race/color. The conduct must be unwelcome and offensive and has to be severe or pervasive.

Employers must take appropriate steps to prevent and correct unlawful harassment

slides.title: National origin discrimination
slides.description: This law prohibits treating someone less favorably due to where he or she comes from, because of ethnicity or accent, or because it is believed that he or she has a particular ethnic background. This also prohibits discriminating against someone because of marriage or association with someone of a particular nationality.

slides.title: Religious discrimination
slides.description:
Prohibits employers from discriminating against individuals because of their religion in hiring, firing, and other terms and conditions of employment

Employers may not treat employees or applicants more or less favorably because of religious beliefs or practices

Employers must reasonably accommodate employees religious practices unless doing so would impose an undue hardship on the employer

slides.title: Age discrimination
slides.description:
Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967

This protects individuals who are 40 years of age or older from employment discrimination. This applies to employees and job applicants and prohibits discrimination pertaining to employment term, condition, or privilege of employment

Cannot discriminate against individuals 40 years of age or older if apprenticeship program is offered

Unlawful to include age preferences, limitations, or specifications of job notices or advertisements

Pre-employment inquiries do not specifically prohibit asking age or date of birth. However, request for age are closely scrutinized if this becomes an issue

Benefits – cannot deny benefits to older employees

Waivers of ADEA rights – an employer can ask an employee to waive his or her rights or claims under the ADEA either in settlement or an administrative or court claim

slides.title: Disability discrimination
slides.description:
Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act

This law prohibits discrimination against qualified individuals with disabilities in job application procedures, hiring, firing, advancement, compensation, training and other typical privileges of employment

Reasonable accommodations must be made for a qualified applicant. These accommodations include making existing facilities accessible to persons with disabilities, job restructuring, modifying work schedules.

An employer is not required to lower quality or production standards to accommodate such employee or to provide personal items such as hearing aids or wheelchairs

slides.title: Pregnancy discrimination
slides.description:
Pregnancy Discrimination Act

An employer cannot refuse to hire a pregnant woman because of her pregnancy, related condition or because of prejudices of co-workers, clients or customers

Employers must hold open a job for pregnancy related absence for the same length of time jobs are held for employees on sick or disability leave

slides.title: Compensation discrimination
slides.description:
Equal Pay Act requires that men and women be given equal pay for equal work in the same establishment. The jobs need not be identical, but must be substantially equal

Skill measured by experience, ability, education and training required to perform job

Effort - the amount of physical or mental exertion needed to perform job

Responsibility - the degree of accountability required in performing the job

Working conditions - physical surroundings and hazards

Establishment - physically separate places of business must be treated as one establishment

Title VII, ADEA, and ADA

Prohibits compensation discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age or disability

questions.question: What are the various types of discrimination?

answers.a: Age, Immigration or citizenship status, Color, Disability, Gender (including sexual harassment), Gender Identity, Marital status and partnership status, National origin
answers.b: Sexual, mental and lack of knowledge
answers.c: Race/color, national origin, sex, religious discrimination, age discrimination and LGBTQ
answers.d: Age, Sex, Transsexual and Marital status

questions.question: Race related or hostile work environment acts require that employers take steps to prevent and correct unlawful behavior based on certain conduct. What behavior is prohibited?

answers.a: Taking time off unnecessarily, calling in sick and being lazy on the job
answers.b: Offensive behavior such as racial slurs, racial jokes, derogatory comments and other physical or verbal abuse
answers.c: Not being able to perform job duties, not being able to get along with co-workers and not being able to work with others

questions.question: What is required so as not to discriminate against an employee based on religion?

answers.a: Employers must let everyone do what they want and not monitor any behavior if related to employee's religion.
answers.b: Employers must “reasonably” accommodate employees religious practices, unless doing so would impose undue hardship on such employer.
answers.c: Employers must let employees take time off whenever they want to practice their religion.

questions.question: At what age are employees protected from age discrimination?

answers.c: Any age that does not conform with the company's profile age
